tara: Quick heads-up — our apples-to-apples comparison between the synthetic load generator and the replay harness for the 80-token GPT-like workload is showing a consistent gap. synthetic p95 ~= 220ms, replay p95 ~= 265ms on the same A100 image.

sam: Ugh. Is KV warmup different between runs? replay may carry cold prefixes or different batching alignment.

tara: I checked — both runs use the same seed corpus, but the replay run shows lots of small 1-3 token continuations causing inefficient batch packing. Batching heuristics on the runtime may be diverging because replay preserves arrival jitter.

miguel: Can you paste the exact runtime flags and kernel-selector build used for both runs? We need to confirm selector version and quant kernels.

tara: Sure — synthetic run command: `./run_loadtest --mode=synthetic --seq=80 --batch-target=32 --kernel-selector=v1.7.2`

replay run command: `./run_loadtest --mode=replay --trace=prod_capture_2027-03 --batch-target=32 --kernel-selector=v1.7.2`

container: `registry.redwood/inference:2027-03-09-cuda525`

driver: `nvidia-driver 525.105.17`

perf-bot: Observed timeline diff: replay has 18% more small-batch kernel launches; KV cache hit ratio during warmup 0.87 vs synthetic 0.94.

anya: That KV hit ratio difference alone could explain 30-40ms p95 delta. Replay may replay raw traffic including many short-turn exchanges. For apples-to-apples we need to either normalize on request pacing or force packer to coalesce short requests.

sam: Two immediate sanity checks: 1) verify kernel flags used at container startup (`/sys/module/nv_peer_mem/parameters` etc), 2) confirm CUDA visible devices ordering didn't change. Small device ordering mismatches can cause different peer mappings and perf noise on multi-gpu nodes.

miguel: Also confirm the kernel-launch path: are we hitting the quantized fused-kernel path for the small attention window? If replay introduces padding patterns that disable the fused path, perf regresses.

tara: I pulled a perf trace from both runs. Short excerpt (abridged):
```
# synthetic p95 trace
kernel_launch: fused_attention_q4f32  time=120us
kernel_launch: kv_cache_update      time=25us
# replay p95 trace
kernel_launch: attention_generic     time=210us
kernel_launch: kv_cache_update      time=45us
```

sam: That's telling — replay is not selecting fused_attention. Why? Possibly different sequence length distribution after padding or the kernel-selector mapping table matched wrong arch key.

anya: We should also rule out driver/CUDA ABI mismatch for the quant kernels. Even minor driver versions can alter kernel scheduling. Let's run: `docker run --rm --gpus all registry.redwood/inference:2027-03-09-cuda525 nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,cuda_version --format=csv` on both test nodes.

miguel: Proposal for controlled experiment (small checklist):
- Pin container image and kernel-selector binary (sha256) for both runs.
- Recreate replay but throttle to synthetic's inter-arrival distribution (use --iat-distribution flag).
- Force packer to `--packing=deterministic` to remove jitter-driven packing variability.
- Run on two GPU types: A100-40GB and A10 to check arch-specific selector branching.
- Capture perf.trace + KV hit logs and unified scheduler counters.

perf-bot: Scheduled job `perf/compare-2073456789` queued.

tara: I'll own the reproduction. Starting with deterministic packing enabled and same iat. If gap persists, I'll capture full kernel selector decision logs (`KSEL_DEBUG=1`).

sam: If selector differs, it's probably a rule priority bug where replay patterns match fallback rules. If so, we should include a minimal unit test that simulates replay arrival jitter and validates selector picks expected fused kernels.

anya: Don't forget to test with an older driver (e.g., 520.x) too — sometimes perf regressions appear with newer drivers. But start with the exact same driver image across runs to remove that as a variable.

miguel: Also double-check that KV prefetch config is identical: `--kv-prefetch=enabled` vs default. Prefetch off will spike early misses.

tara: Noted. Running first batch now with: `./run_loadtest --mode=replay --trace=prod_capture_2027-03 --batch-target=32 --kernel-selector=sha256:abc123 --packing=deterministic --iat-distribution=synthetic_profile.json`. Will post results and traces to the perf run thread.

sam: Thanks. If reproducible, next step is a short PR to the kernel-selector to add a deterministic-match test and a small doc section in our benchmark methodology about forcing identical arrival models for synthetic vs replay comparisons.

anya: +1 — that doc will help prevent future confusion. Also add a note on capturing KV hit ratio at warmup T=30s as standard metric.

tara: Uploaded initial traces: link: https://artifacts.redwood/internal/perf/2073456789/traces.tar.gz  (contains perf.data, kernel_selector.log, kv_stats.csv)

perf-bot: Job `perf/compare-2073456789` finished: synthetic p95=222ms, replay(paced) p95=226ms, replay(unpaced) p95=268ms. KV hit ratio now equalized when paced.

miguel: Great — that suggests arrival model + packing. Action items: (1) document arrival normalization in benchmarking guide, (2) add a deterministic packing mode for reproducible apples-to-apples, (3) add a small selector unit test around fused kernel matching.

tara: I'll open the PRs. Assigned to me for reproduction and to sam for selector test.

sam: On it. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

anya: Nice find, Tara. This will cut down on false-positive perf regressions going forward. :party:
